title: FTSE Russell — preliminary December 2026 additions/deletions published (four weeks before implementation)
source: EST: owner-published, stated on TWO primaries this session and cross-checked against the rule. (1) FTSE Russell's reconstitution page, lseg.com/en/ftse-russell/russell-reconstitution, fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 228,333 bytes, 13,561 characters extracted in-session), verbatim: "Beginning on November 13, the preliminary lists are communicated to the marketplace, and updates are provided on November 20, November 27, and December 4", and in its FAQ "Preliminary lists for the upcoming December 2026 Reconstitution will be communicated beginning November 13, with updates on November 20, November 27, December 4, and December 11." (2) FTSE Russell, "FAQ Document Russell US Equity 2026", July 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents PDF, HTTP 200, 198,134 bytes, text-extracted in-session), whose dated December 2026 calendar column gives "Indicative Review Products circulated | 13 November 2026" and "Release of Russell Enhanced Indicative Review File (REIR) | 13 November 2026", with the query period running "16 November 2026 to 27 November 2026" and lock-down opening 30 November 2026. (3) RULE CHECK: ground rules v7.2 (August 2026) Appendix F gives the December leg "Preliminary Information Released = Four weeks prior to implementation"; 2026-11-13 to 2026-12-11 is exactly 28 days, and the FAQ's own 2-week query + 2-week lockdown sums to the same four weeks. Filed estimate because a proposal is always estimate by contract and this calendar's confirmed-tier prefixes have no member for an index owner's own published schedule. Promote when this calendar gains such a prefix. Discovered during the russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11 initial research (2026-09-06), and it is the INFORMATION event where 2026-12-11 is the EXECUTION event -- a calendar that tracks only the latter cannot see the former. WHY THE PROPOSER CARES, specifically: the open question on the December leg is how much of the Russell 2000's ~12.8%-of-base-market-value annual reconstitution turnover (the owner's own 2004-2026 average, 252 stocks) actually lands in December now that the schedule is semi-annual. The 2026-11-13 preliminary lists ANSWER that directly -- they publish the additions, deletions and indicative shares/float -- with no macro confound at all, whereas 2026-12-11 itself sits inside a corridor of 22 tracked events including a government-funding deadline, a CR expiry, CPI-1 and FOMC-2. The proposer measured that the confound is fatal to the alternative: on 20 years of December second Fridays with NO reconstitution, IWM's whole-day volume ratio to its own trailing-60d median already exceeded 1.20x in 5 of 20 years, so a volume threshold on 12-11 carries a 25% false-positive rate before the funding deadline is even counted. The preliminary-list count is the low-noise instrument and it prints 28 days earlier. Registered as the proposer's scored forward test FT-russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11-1. Note that this is the direct December analogue of russell-recon-preliminary-2027-05-21, proposed by the russell-reconstitution-2027-06-25 lane on the same day for the June 2027 leg; the two conventions differ (four weeks in December, five in June) and both are confirmed exact against published instances. Impact low: it is a data publication, it moves no forced flow of its own, and it licenses nothing -- it is tracked because it is where the December scope question gets settled. The proposer deliberately did NOT propose the rank day 2026-10-30, though it is equally dated and equally owner-published ("the rank day for the December reconstitution falls on Friday, October 30"): membership is determined on rank day but nothing is disclosed, so it is an internal cut-off rather than an event a reader could act on or measure.
